Including inputs from safety assessments such as more detailed CO dispersion analysis results. 2  Review rail car delivery activities and how it impacts site access during periods of connecting and disconnecting rail cars to site; engaging rail operator to understand any restrictive requirements not considered so far.  Input into PTB / civil engineers’ site grading and drainage plan, to consider elevating certain equipment to protect for potential storm surge or flooding and better taking into account dispersion of potential CO leaks and any concentration effects in low-lying areas. 2  Consider requirements for CO pipeline reception facilities such as pigging (launcher / receiver) 2  Focus on modularization and the use of pre-assembled units (PAU) to reduce on site construction complexity and duration. 4.6 OTHER REQUIRED UTILITIES 4.6.1 INSTRUMENT AIR The instrument air system consists of 2x2,000 m3/h air compressor packages, 2x2,000 m3/h air dryer packages, and 2x100 m3 instrument air receivers. The air receiver is designed to provide a 15-minute supply of instrument air in the event of a compressor shutdown. The spare air compressor, air dryer, and air receiver will be utilized for purging purposes. 4.6.2 NITROGEN There are no specific nitrogen consumers identified in this study phase. However, a small nitrogen flow may be required by the CO analyzer package(s). When needed, nitrogen will be supplied to consumers 2 from nitrogen bottles. 4.6.3 POTABLE WATER It is expected that a potable water supply will be sourced from a connection to the local water main. Identified potable water users include safety showers, eye wash stations and utility stations, and building sprinkler systems. It is likely that some fire hydrants will be required at key locations on the site (refer to Section 8.3.4, Fire Fighting and Water Supply). PTB’s subcontractor GHD has made provisions for a single fire hydrant in a central area between the liquefaction trains and storage tanks, fed by a dedicated new 6” pipe tapped into the street main line, as shown in their plans in Appendix A.
